questions.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes BP 220 socialized vs. economic housing by target income?

rationale.c: Overstates the economic housing upper limit; also confuses with middle-income categories
rationale.d: Incorrectly combines both categories into one income bracket
rationale.correct: BP 220 Revised IRR Rule II Sec. 3 defines socialized housing for families with gross annual income ≤ P200,000; economic housing P200,001–P4,000,000 annually
rationale.takeaway: Socialized = ≤70k/month; Economic = 70k–120k/month. These income brackets determine lot and floor area minimums.

questions.text: A 4-hectare socialized row house housing project in Manila proposes 1,200 units. What is the minimum total lot area required to comply with BP 220?

rationale.a: Miscalculation: confuses the minimum per unit (28 sqm) with number of units
rationale.b: This applies if using the socialized single detached standard (64 sqm) instead of row house (28 sqm)
rationale.d: This is the total site area, not the minimum lot requirement
rationale.correct: BP 220 socialized row house = 28 sqm/unit. 1,200 units × 28 sqm = 33,600 sqm required. Available 40,000 sqm (4 hectares) ≥ 33,600 sqm ✓
rationale.takeaway: For row house computation: Total units × 28 sqm/unit = minimum lot area. Always check housing type to select the right minimum.

questions.text: Under BP 220 Revised IRR Table 7, what is the minimum lot area for a socialized housing single detached unit?

rationale.a: 28 sqm is the minimum lot area for socialized row houses per Table 7, not single detached (64 sqm) (ERR-DSGN: confusing housing types).
rationale.c: 72 sqm is the minimum for ECONOMIC single detached, not socialized. Students commonly confuse these two categories.
rationale.d: 48 sqm is the minimum for socialized DUPLEX/SINGLE ATTACHED units, not single detached.
rationale.correct: BP 220 Revised IRR Table 7 specifies 64 sqm minimum lot area for socialized housing single detached units.
rationale.takeaway: Socialized SD = 64 sqm; Economic SD = 72 sqm. The 72 sqm value is economic, NOT socialized. Always check category AND housing type.

questions.text: A senior living facility in Cebu develops 300 economic housing units (BP 220) on a 3.5-hectare site. Calculate the net buildable area available if 25% of the site is allocated to roads and amenities.

rationale.a: This omits the calculation—27.5% of site incorrectly calculated
rationale.d: This is gross site area, not accounting for roads/amenities deduction
rationale.correct: Net buildable = 35,000 sqm × (1 − 0.25) = 35,000 × 0.75 = 26,250 sqm available for housing blocks
rationale.takeaway: Always deduct roads and common amenities (typically 20–30%) from gross site area before computing unit count or lot requirement compliance.

questions.text: A developer purchases a 3-hectare site in Pasig for socialized row house housing. After excluding 30% for roads and common spaces, how many units can be developed while maintaining BP 220 compliance?

rationale.a: Miscalculation; ~980 would require a larger site or misapplication of deduction.
rationale.c: Too low; assumes a 2-hectare site (20,000 sqm × 0.70 = 14,000 ÷ 28 = 500 units) instead of 3-hectare.
rationale.d: Overstates density; would require lot area < 28 sqm or a much larger site.
rationale.correct: Net buildable = 30,000 sqm × 0.70 = 21,000 sqm. Units = 21,000 ÷ 28 sqm/lot = 750 units ✓. This maintains BP 220 compliance (28 sqm minimum lot for socialized row house).
rationale.takeaway: Row house density: (Gross site × net% buildable) ÷ 28 sqm/unit. For 3 hectares at 70% buildable: 21,000 ÷ 28 = 750 units.

questions.text: For the senior living project above (300 economic single detached units, 26,250 sqm buildable), verify BP 220 compliance. Which statement is correct?

options.text: 300 units × 72 sqm/lot = 21,600 sqm required; project is compliant (21,600 < 26,250 sqm available)
300 units × 72 sqm/lot = 21,600 sqm required; project is compliant because site is 35,000 sqm gross
300 units × 22 sqm/floor = 6,600 sqm required; project is compliant with margin for amenities
Economic housing requires 64 sqm per lot, so 300 × 64 = 19,200 sqm is required

rationale.b: While the calculation is correct, the reasoning is wrong — compliance must be checked against NET buildable area (after roads/amenities deduction), not gross site area
rationale.c: Confuses floor area (22 sqm economic) with lot area (72 sqm economic SD); lot area determines site density, not floor area alone
rationale.d: 64 sqm applies to SOCIALIZED single detached, not economic; confuses the two categories
rationale.correct: BP 220 economic SD = 72 sqm/unit (lot area per Table 7). 300 × 72 = 21,600 sqm required. 21,600 < 26,250 sqm buildable = compliant.
rationale.takeaway: Compliance uses NET buildable area (after roads/amenities), and LOT area minimums (not floor area) determine unit count feasibility. Economic SD = 72 sqm lot.

questions.text: A 1.5-hectare socialized single detached housing project has an average unit floor area of 28 sqm. Calculate the gross density (occupants per hectare) assuming 5 occupants per unit.

rationale.a: Miscalculates unit count; may use 48 sqm/lot (duplex) instead of 64 sqm (SD)
rationale.c: Uses row house standard (28 sqm) resulting in ~357 units/hectare × 5 = 1,785 persons/hectare (wrong housing type)
rationale.d: Severely undercounts; may confuse with parking density or other metric
rationale.correct: Units per hectare = 10,000 sqm ÷ 64 sqm/lot ≈ 156 units/hectare. Density = 156 × 5 occupants ≈ 781 persons/hectare
rationale.takeaway: Density = (10,000 ÷ lot minimum) × occupants per unit. For socialized SD: (10,000 ÷ 64) × 5 ≈ 781 persons/hectare gross.

questions.text: A developer proposes a mixed-income project: 500 socialized SD units (64 sqm/lot) and 200 economic SD units (72 sqm/lot), plus 35% of site for roads/amenities. What minimum total site area (in hectares) is required?

rationale.a: Underestimates; may only count socialized lots without economic or misapply the 35% deduction
rationale.c: Significantly underestimates; may use row house minimums (28 sqm) instead of SD (64 sqm) for socialized
rationale.d: Close but may use net area instead of gross or miscalculate one component
rationale.correct: Socialized SD required: 500 × 64 = 32,000 sqm. Economic SD required: 200 × 72 = 14,400 sqm. Total net lot area = 46,400 sqm. Roads/amenities = 35% of gross, so buildable = 65%. Gross site = 46,400 ÷ 0.65 = 71,385 sqm ≈ 7.14 hectares. Closest option: 7.08 hectares.
rationale.takeaway: Mixed-income site: (socialized units × socialized lot) + (economic units × economic lot) = net buildable. Divide by (1 − road%) for gross site. Socialized SD = 64 sqm; Economic SD = 72 sqm.

questions.text: What is the minimum floor area per unit for both socialized and economic housing under BP 220?

options.text: Socialized = 28 sqm; Economic = 72 sqm, which is typically required for larger family units
Both = 30 sqm, as mandated for mixed-use developments
Socialized = 22 sqm; Economic = 42 sqm, often applied in urban redevelopment zones

rationale.b: Confuses LOT area minimums (28 sqm row house lot, 72 sqm economic SD lot) with FLOOR area minimums.
rationale.c: Oversimplifies and does not match BP 220 standards.
rationale.d: These are commonly cited incorrect values; 22 sqm is actually the economic floor area, and 42 sqm does not appear in the official IRR floor area table.
rationale.correct: BP 220 Revised IRR specifies minimum FLOOR area: Socialized = 18 sqm; Economic = 22 sqm per single-family dwelling unit.
rationale.takeaway: Floor area: Socialized = 18 sqm; Economic = 22 sqm. Do NOT confuse with lot area (64/48/28 socialized; 72/54/36 economic).

questions.text: Under PD 1096, what occupancy group classification applies to a multi-unit senior residential facility where each unit is individually owned?

options.text: Group A-1 (single-family), typically used for detached homes
Group D (institutional), which is generally for hospitals and similar facilities
Group B (hotel/dormitory), often applied to transient accommodations

rationale.a: A-1 applies to single-family detached structures, not multi-unit residential
rationale.c: Group D (institutional) applies to facilities with resident care staff (nursing homes with 24/7 care); owner-occupied multi-family = A-2
rationale.d: Group B (transient hotel/dormitory) applies when units are not permanently occupied by same residents
rationale.correct: PD 1096 Section 303 classifies multi-family residences as Group A-2. Individual ownership of residential units = A-2, regardless of occupant age
rationale.takeaway: Multi-family residential = Group A-2 per PD 1096, even for seniors. Group D requires licensed institutional care with resident staff.
